A1.justification: Both PDFs describe revisions of the same graph anomaly detection work, with PAF revised into APF. The complete papers, including v1 Appendices A–E and v3 Appendices A–L, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PAF evaluations on ten datasets, component ablations, coefficient visualizations, and supervision and hyperparameter analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 reports original APF evaluations and ablations, plus unsupervised detection, representation visualization, efficiency measurements, and training-strategy comparisons.

M1.justification: v3 replaces v1's fixed adjacency/Laplacian filters with learnable Chebyshev polynomial filters. Its high-pass pre-training objective uses node-specific, Rayleigh Quotient-selected subgraph summaries instead of a global summary (Sections 3.1 versus 4.1). The feature-based gated fusion and class-specific regularization already existed in v1 and are retained.

E1.justification: The ten benchmark datasets and application domains remain unchanged. v3 Appendix I.1 adds a fully label-free detection scenario on three retained datasets—Reddit, Weibo, and DGraph—using pretrained representations with Isolation Forest, extending v1's semi-supervised evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain all 17 earlier baselines and add ACM, FAGCN, AdaGNN, GAS, SpaceGNN, XGBGraph, and BWDGI. The new unsupervised comparison includes raw-feature Isolation Forest and published GAD-EBM and DiffGAD results. Within the varying-supervision comparison, BWGNN is added and GRACE is removed.

E3.justification: The core 100-label setting, three detection metrics, and 800/500-epoch budgets remain. However, the reported representation search narrows from 32–512 dimensions to {32, 64}, and filter-order settings replace layer-depth settings. v3 removes the one-anomaly supervision point and introduces homophily-quartile evaluation, an unsupervised IF protocol, time/memory measurements, and joint-training controls.

E4.justification: v3 adds RQ-selected versus full-neighborhood/no-subgraph ablations, no-pre-training and joint-versus-two-stage controls, homophily-quartile analyses, t-SNE visualizations, and efficiency comparisons. It removes v1's separate G-BT+PAF and GRACE+PAF ablation suites and scalar/vector fusion ablations. Hyperparameter analysis now covers all three metrics for APF rather than AUROC across three PAF instantiations.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over ten supplied random splits and use the same ± reporting practice in performance and ablation tables. v3 introduces no new seed-count disclosure, confidence-interval procedure, or significance testing; additional result rows do not change that practice.

E6.justification: v1's three PAF integration result sets are replaced by APF results under revised architecture and search settings, while all 17 shared baseline rows retain their values across the three main metrics. New experiments add substantial outcomes: for example, v3 Table 5 reports DGraph AUROC of 63.3±0.6 for IF with pre-training versus 60.9±0.7 for raw-feature IF. Quartile, efficiency, and joint-training results are also new.

T1.justification: v1's spectral-energy and spectral-regression-loss propositions and proofs are removed. v3 revises ASBM and its separability argument to incorporate degree parameters, explicit class priors, concentration bounds, and a prior-adjusted separator (Section 3.3 and Appendix E). It also introduces the cited Rayleigh Quotient lemma, polynomial-filter construction, and time-complexity derivations. These are substantive mathematical revisions, not relocated proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from a plug-and-play enhancement demonstrated with several pre-training objectives to a dedicated anomaly-aware framework using RQ-selected subgraphs and learnable filters. v3 explicitly claims mitigation of node- and class-level homophily disparity. Adaptive fusion and effectiveness under limited supervision remain central claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting RQ to feature–structure inconsistency and attributing joint-training disadvantages to competing objectives. Appendix D discusses weaker performance than XGBGraph on feature-dominated datasets. Appendix J explicitly distinguishes Gaussian features, oracle filter assignments, and linear theory from the learned APF architecture. These substantive applicability qualifications were absent from v1.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents branch standardization, one-hop sampling exceptions for Amazon/T-Finance/T-Social, and a practical reduced search for regularization targets. It changes the stated code location from the anonymous PAF repository to the named APF GitHub repository and supplies runtime/memory measurements. Hardware, software frameworks, optimizer, and main training budgets remain documented as before.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against recent unsupervised, limited-label, cross-domain, and generalist GAD research. It distinguishes APF's single-graph setting from auxiliary-network approaches and explicitly contrasts its use of UniGAD's RQ sampler with UniGAD's multi-level task unification. Polynomial-filter borrowing is also made central to the method's relationship with prior work.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and methodology are extensively rewritten around anomaly awareness and dual-granularity disparity. The standalone Motivation section and RQ1–RQ5 experiment organization disappear; theoretical insights move into methodology, and the appendices are substantially reorganized. This exceeds a terminology change from PAF to APF.

P2.justification: The paper switches from two-column ACM formatting to single-column ICLR formatting. The architecture diagram is redrawn, the filtering toy figure is removed, and new quartile plots, t-SNE panels, and experimental tables appear. Benchmark tables gain average columns and different row organization; supervision plots change from bars to lines. Retained coefficient heatmaps show six rather than eight dimensions.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v3 provides stronger empirical scrutiny through RQ-specific controls, stronger baselines, training-strategy comparisons, and explicit applicability limitations. However, its expanded proof does not establish why the feature-distance condition controls the added inverse-distance prior correction (Appendix E). The efficiency discussion also overgeneralizes Table 6, where APF uses more T-Social memory than ConsisGAD and SpaceGNN. These gains and unresolved theoretical and interpretive weaknesses leave the net quality change uncertain.
